title: PostgreSQL WAL disk full halted all transaction writes
summary: The write-ahead log (WAL) disk space for the PostgreSQL database was full, causing all transaction writes to be halted, impacting 500,000 transactions and resulting in a potential revenue loss of $25,000.

timeline.event: PagerDuty alert fired - alert threshold reached 90% of disk space used, triggering an alert.
on-call acknowledged, initial investigation - confirmed PostgreSQL WAL disk full and initiated remediation steps.
root cause identified - WAL autovacuum was not configured to run, leading to excessive log accumulation.
remediation applied - resized the WAL disk volume and restarted the PostgreSQL service.
service restored, error rate back to baseline - transaction writes resumed without further issues.

root_cause: The PostgreSQL WAL disk was full due to a misconfiguration of autovacuum, which did not run to clear the logs, causing the disk space to fill up over time.
contributing_factors: Misconfigured autovacuum settings
Insufficient monitoring of disk space usage
resolution_steps: Executed `ALTER SYSTEM SET autovacuum_max_workers TO 4;` to increase the number of autovacuum workers.
Resized the WAL disk volume from 10GB to 50GB using `ALTER DATABASE payment_db SET DEFAULT_WAL_RETENTION to '3d';` and `ALTER DATABASE payment_db SET wal_level to 'replica';`.
Restarted the PostgreSQL service to apply the changes.
lessons_learned: Improper configuration of autovacuum can lead to disk space issues
Regular monitoring of disk space and tuning autovacuum settings are critical for database health

action_items.action: Implement automated disk space monitoring and alerts
Review and update autovacuum configuration
